title: Atomic Habits
author: James Clear
description: Practical guidance on building useful habits through small changes, supportive environments, and consistent routines.

title: The Alchemist
author: Paulo Coelho
description: A young shepherd travels in search of treasure and discovers lessons about purpose, courage, and following his dreams.

title: Clean Code
author: Robert C. Martin
description: A guide to writing readable and maintainable software, covering naming, functions, testing, and refactoring.

title: The Psychology of Money
author: Morgan Housel
description: Essays exploring how personal experience, behaviour, patience, and uncertainty shape financial decisions.

title: Clean Architecture
author: Robert C. Martin
description: Explores software boundaries, dependencies, and design principles for systems that remain adaptable as requirements change.

title: The Pragmatic Programmer
author: David Thomas and Andrew Hunt
description: Practical advice on problem solving, automation, collaboration, and developing reliable software with professional care.

title: Refactoring
author: Martin Fowler
description: Explains how to improve existing code through small structural changes while preserving its behaviour.

title: Design Patterns
author: Erich Gamma, Richard Helm, Ralph Johnson and John Vlissides
description: Reusable object-oriented design approaches, explaining the problems they address and their trade-offs.

title: Pride and Prejudice
author: Jane Austen
description: Elizabeth Bennet navigates family expectations, social class, and first impressions as her relationship with Mr Darcy develops.

title: Jane Eyre
author: Charlotte Bronte
description: An orphaned young woman becomes a governess and seeks love and independence while confronting difficult moral choices.

title: The Great Gatsby
author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
description: Nick Carraway observes the wealthy world of Jay Gatsby, where ambition, lost love, and social status collide.

author: George Orwell
description: Winston Smith lives under a totalitarian regime that controls information, language, and private life.

title: Animal Farm
author: George Orwell
description: Farm animals overthrow their owner, but their hopes for equality are undermined by a new hierarchy of power.

title: The Hobbit
author: J. R. R. Tolkien
description: Bilbo Baggins accompanies a band of dwarves on a journey toward a dragon-guarded treasure.

title: Frankenstein
author: Mary Shelley
description: A scientist creates a living being and then abandons it, beginning a story about responsibility, isolation, and revenge.

title: Dracula
author: Bram Stoker
description: A group of friends confronts Count Dracula in a gothic story told through letters, diaries, and other records.

title: Little Women
author: Louisa May Alcott
description: The four March sisters grow up together, balancing family responsibilities with their different ambitions and hopes.

title: A Christmas Carol
author: Charles Dickens
description: Ebenezer Scrooge is visited by spirits who challenge him to reconsider his treatment of others and the direction of his life.

title: The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
author: Arthur Conan Doyle
description: Cases in which Sherlock Holmes and Dr Watson investigate puzzles through observation and deduction.

title: The Time Machine
author: H. G. Wells
description: An inventor travels into the distant future and encounters societies that raise questions about progress and inequality.
